title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page sets out an axiomatic framework, in a weak form, for a multiplicative resolution of the constant sheaf on a topos.

Setting. X is a topos and k a commutative base ring. C* is a resolution of the constant sheaf k:
0 -> k -> C^0 -> C^1 -> C^2 -> ...
The unit section of k gives a section 1 of C^0. Write Z^i = ker(d) for the cocycles in C^i and B^i = im(d) for the coboundaries.

The key point is that C* is not required to be a dg-algebra. Grothendieck asks only for bilinear pairings in which one factor is a cocycle:
- a_{ij}: Z^i x C^j -> C^{i+j}
- b_{ij}: C^i x Z^j -> C^{i+j}

These are subject to four axioms.
1. a_{ij} and b_{ij} agree on Z^i x Z^j and land in Z^{i+j}. So x∘y is unambiguous and is defined as soon as dx = 0 or dy = 0.
2. Associativity (x∘y)∘z = x∘(y∘z) holds whenever two of the three factors are cocycles, which makes every product defined. Also 1∘x = x∘1 = x.
3. Strict graded commutativity: x∘y = (-1)^{deg x deg y} y∘x. Moreover x∘x = 0 for x a cocycle of odd degree.
4. Leibniz rule in the only form that makes sense. For i, j >= 1 there is a commutative square
   C^{i-1} x Z^j --b--> C^{i+j-1}
   (d x id) | ......... | d
   B^i x Z^j --a--> Z^{i+j}
   that is, d(x∘z) = dx∘z for z a cocycle. In particular B·Z ⊂ B. The mirror rule d(z∘x) = (-1)^j z∘dx follows from axiom 3.

Consequence. These axioms are exactly what is needed to make H^*(C) (and, with acyclic C^i, presumably H^*(X,k)) a graded-commutative k-algebra in which odd classes square to zero.

The struck-out lines and the closing NB try to interpret this data, or its defect, via Hom_k(C^i ⊗_k Z^j, Z^{i+j+1}). This looks like a first attempt to describe the ambiguity or homotopy in these partial products.

Purpose. Given the cote ("Complexe de De Rham à puissances divisées", IHÉS 1976), this is very likely the prelude to adding divided powers γ_n on even cocycles. The aim would be an axiomatic notion of a 'PD-multiplicative resolution', abstracting what de Rham and PD-de Rham complexes give in crystalline theory. Under that structure cohomology inherits divided powers on even degrees.

The next-page transcription (a Sullivan-style text on nilmanifolds) seems to be an unrelated inserted document. The page number written on the sheet is 349.
errors: No acyclicity hypothesis (flasque, or Γ-acyclic C^i) is stated. Without it, the product on H^*(Γ(X,C*)) need not compute the cup product on H^*(X,k). This may be intended implicitly.

Axiom 3 (x∘x = 0 strictly for odd cocycles), together with acyclicity and compatibility with cup product, is very restrictive. Example: X = classifying topos of Z/2 (or RP^∞) with k = F_2. The degree-1 generator x has x^2 = Sq^1 x ≠ 0, so no such resolution computing H^*(X,F_2) can exist there. The axioms thus implicitly single out 'de Rham-type' cohomologies, where Steenrod-type obstructions vanish. The page does not comment on this.
Axiom 3 must be read only where the product is defined (one factor a cocycle). Axiom 2 needs 'at least two cocycles' to guarantee definedness; both points are fine but only implicit.

ideas.what: Axiomatics of a resolution of k on a topos carrying only partial products (one factor a cocycle), with associativity, strict graded commutativity and a Leibniz rule
ideas.modern_name: partial / weak multiplicative structure on a resolution; compare partial algebras (Kriz–May), 'multiplicative resolutions' for cup products in sheaf cohomology (Godement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Godement (cup products via resolutions, 1958); partial algebras: Kriz–May (1995)
ideas.where_published: Possibly reflected in the 1976 IHÉS lecture material on PD de Rham complexes; not in EGA/SGA as far as known

ideas.what: Strict alternation x∘x = 0 for odd cocycles as an axiom, presumably preparing divided powers on even cocycles
ideas.modern_name: strictly graded-commutative (PD) cochain models; divided power structure on de Rham / crystalline cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot, Illusie (PD de Rham complexes, crystalline cohomology, 1970s)
ideas.where_published: Crystal ideas in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968); this axiomatics specifically unsure

ideas.what: Interpreting the structure via Hom_k(C^i ⊗ Z^j, Z^{i+j+1})
ideas.modern_name: homotopy / obstruction data for multiplicative structures (A∞ / E∞-type corrections)

missed.claim: Requiring strict alternation on odd cocycles (and presumably divided powers on even ones) of a resolution of k on a topos implicitly separates de Rham / crystalline-type cohomology from Betti / étale mod p cohomology. In the latter, Steenrod operations (x^2 = Sq^n x, x^p = P^n x) obstruct such structures. Grothendieck's axiomatics would thus be an early abstract framing of 'Steenrod operations vanish (or are replaced by divided powers) on de Rham-type cohomology'. That theme has resurfaced in recent work on Steenrod-type operations on de Rham cohomology in characteristic p (precise references unsure).

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a minimal axiomatic criterion, in terms of a resolution with partial products, for when a topos cohomology carries PD structure. This is a possibly useful lens on E∞ versus strictly commutative models in characteristic p. It is only implicit here and not developed on the page.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would amount to a homotopy-coherent treatment of partial multiplicative resolutions. However, it is fully subsumed by modern E∞/A∞ theory, so its novelty is low.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but essentially routine axiomatization of the minimal product structure on a resolution needed to get a graded-commutative cohomology ring. Its interest lies in the context (PD de Rham complexes) and the implicit tension with Steenrod operations, which the page does not discuss.
transcription_corrections: The page number written at bottom left is 349, not 347.
'bilin.' is an insertion above 'Accouplements', i.e. 'Accouplements bilinéaires (notés x,y ↦ x∘y)'.
The bracketed note after the cases is probably 'i,j ≥ 0'.
In 2°, the illegible text after the associativity formula is probably 'pour trois sections locales x, y, z (de C^i, C^j, C^k) dont deux sont des cocycles'.
The interlinear insertion under 3° reads roughly 'si x section locale de C^i, y section locale de Z^j ... bilin.' (partly uncertain).
In 4°, the boxed diagram has B^i × Z^j → Z^{i+j} on top, with vertical arrows d×id and d from C^{i-1}×Z^j → C^{i+j-1} (labelled b_{ij}); the side note reads 'd(x∘z) = dx∘z'.
